quote.text: And keep in mind too that pain often comes in disguise—as drowsiness, fever, loss of appetite.… When you’re bothered by things like that, remind yourself: “I’m giving in to pain.
quote.author: Marcus Aurelius
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Recognize that your own discomfort or fatigue may be masking a deeper struggle, and approach both your own and your child's small troubles with compassion instead of immediate frustration.
    • Understand that, much like hidden pain, children sometimes express their inner needs through subtle behaviors; by attuning to these signals, you foster a nurturing and empathetic environment.
  • Leadership
    • In leadership, one must differentiate between external challenges and those internal feelings that arise from within; acknowledging these can help you lead with clarity instead of being overwhelmed by transient setbacks.
    • Use the awareness that pain often disguises itself to empathize with your team, encouraging them to address underlying issues before they manifest as larger conflicts.
  • Product Management
    • Much like understanding disguised pain, a good product manager discerns whether features are underperforming due to surface issues or deeper misalignments with user needs.
    • Reflect on feedback and data with the mindset that apparent market or user resistance might be masking fundamental problems, prompting a thoughtful reassessment rather than a hasty solution.
